title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 140-3, 'variations sur l'équation des lacets', the sequel to La Longue Marche). Grothendieck starts from datum (1): a (profinite) group 𝔊 with two distinguished elements ρ, σ and an extra element τ' (an orientation-reversing 'reflection'). The model is the profinite completion of the modular group or of a triangle/cartographic group, with ρ and σ the elliptic generators of the vertex and edge stabilizers. The data split into the following pieces.
- 𝔊^+ is the orientation-preserving index-≤2 subgroup.
- G_{ρ,σ} is a group containing 𝔊^+ as a normal subgroup and acting on it. Each g ∈ G_{ρ,σ} sends ρ to a 𝔊^+-conjugate of ρ^{ε'} and σ to a 𝔊^+-conjugate of σ^{ε}. Here ε' = ε'_G(g) and ε = ε_G(g).
- Γ_{ρ,σ} = G_{ρ,σ}/𝔊^+ is the 'outer' group, an analogue of a Galois or Grothendieck–Teichmüller type group.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} carries a cyclotomic-type character χ_γ : Γ_{ρ,σ} → Ẑ^*.
- Γ_{ρ,σ} also carries two sign characters, recording whether γ inverts the procyclic subgroups L_ρ = ⟨ρ⟩ and L_σ = ⟨σ⟩ up to conjugacy.

The previous page introduces the normalizer groups. N^*_ρ ⊂ N_ρ and N^*_σ ⊂ N_σ are the elements whose sign on L_ρ (resp. L_σ) agrees with ε'_G (resp. ε_G). The maps δ_ρ = δ_G∘i_ρ : N^*_ρ → Γ and δ_σ = δ_G∘i_σ : N^*_σ → Γ are epimorphisms. The exact diagrams (41) and (43) compare 1→Z_ρ→N^*_ρ→{±1}→1 with 1→Γ'→Γ→{±1}→1, and likewise for σ.

This page does three things.
1. Notational NB. The names ε_γ and ε'_γ : Γ_{ρ,σ}→{±1} are misleading, because the unprimed one refers to the action on L_σ rather than L_ρ. Grothendieck proposes ε_{γ,ρ}, ε_{γ,σ}, or simply ε_ρ, ε_σ. Clashing with the homomorphisms of the same name on N^*_ρ, N^*_σ is harmless when ρ^2 ≠ 1 and σ^2 ≠ 1, because then (41) and (43) make the two meanings compatible.
2. Summary diagram (45). Starting from (𝔊, ρ, σ, τ') one has built 𝔊^+, G_{ρ,σ}, Γ_{ρ,σ}, Z_{ρ,σ}, N^*_ρ, N^*_σ. They fit in a commutative diagram:
   - the extension 1→𝔊^+→G_{ρ,σ}→Γ_{ρ,σ}→1;
   - 𝔊^+ ⊂ 𝔊 → G_{ρ,σ};
   - L_0 ≃ SZ_{ρ,σ} → Z_{ρ,σ}, SN^*_ρ → N^*_ρ and SN^*_σ → N^*_σ, all landing in 𝔊^+ and G_{ρ,σ} respectively;
   - dashed epimorphisms δ_Z, δ_ρ, δ_σ onto Γ_{ρ,σ};
   - the 'character map' Γ_{ρ,σ} → Ẑ^* × {±1} × {±1}, γ ↦ (χ_γ, ε_{γ,ρ}, ε_{γ,σ}).
3. Definitions (46). SZ_{ρ,σ} is the image of L_0 in Z_{ρ,σ}, equal to Ker(δ_Z). SN_ρ = Ker(δ_ρ) = Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ) and SN_σ = Ker(δ_σ) = Cent_{𝔊^+}(σ). This holds because an element of N^*_ρ lying in 𝔊^+ has ε'_G = +1, so it must fix ρ rather than invert it, granted that normalizers act on L_ρ through ±1. A margin note suggests calling these SZ_ρ, SZ_σ.

So each δ is a 'lifting' of the outer group Γ to the normalizer of a cyclic inertia-type subgroup. The kernels are centralizers, giving 1 → Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ) → N^*_ρ → Γ → 1, as made explicit on the next page (47). This is the group-theoretic skeleton for studying Γ (a GT-like or Galois-like group) through its action on 'tangential base points' at the cusps and elliptic points ρ, σ.
errors: Notational inconsistency: (46) writes SN'_ρ, SN'_σ (and the sentence lists N'_ρ, N'_σ), while diagram (45) and the next page use SN^*_ρ, SN^*_σ; the primes are evidently meant as stars.

Ker(δ_ρ) = Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ) tacitly assumes that elements of N_ρ act on L_ρ only through ±1. For a procyclic L_ρ the full Aut is larger, so this needs the setup's hypotheses, e.g. ρ of finite order with appropriate rigidity. The next page's (47bis) phrase 'Im(SN_ρ→𝔊^+) = Norm_{𝔊^+}(L_ρ)' sits in mild tension with the centralizer statement unless ρ^2 ≠ 1 is used.
The NB reverses the expected naming (unprimed ε_γ ↔ L_σ); Grothendieck himself flags this as confusing and proposes a correction.

ideas.what: Outer extension 1→𝔊^+→G_{ρ,σ}→Γ_{ρ,σ}→1 with a character map Γ→Ẑ^*×{±1}×{±1} (cyclotomic character plus two inversion signs)
ideas.modern_name: Outer Galois-type action on a profinite triangle/modular group; GT-type groups with cyclotomic character
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), Drinfeld/Ihara for GT; Belyi for the Galois side
ideas.where_published: Ideas in the spirit of the Esquisse d'un programme and La Longue Marche; this specific diagram is not known to be published

ideas.what: Normalizers of the procyclic subgroups ⟨ρ⟩, ⟨σ⟩ with a sign-compatibility condition surject onto the outer group, with kernel the centralizer in 𝔊^+
ideas.modern_name: Lifting outer actions to tangential/inertia base points (normalizers of inertia/elliptic subgroups)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne, Ihara, Nakamura on tangential base points and inertia normalizers)

ideas.what: Notational refinement ε_{γ,ρ}, ε_{γ,σ}, compatible with ε_ρ, ε_σ on normalizers when ρ^2≠1, σ^2≠1

deep.surprise_reason: A summary and bookkeeping page: a commutative diagram recapitulating previously constructed groups, plus a notational correction. The underlying structure (outer actions, normalizers of elliptic/inertia subgroups, centralizer kernels) is standard in anabelian/GT theory and nothing new is claimed here.
transcription_corrections: The group in 'de (1) i.e. de 𝔖 muni de ρ, σ, τ'' and in 𝔖^+ is written as Grothendieck's script 𝔊 (consistent with the neighbouring pages), not 𝔖.
Margin note reads: 'NB On peut donc aussi les noter SZ_ρ, SZ_σ au lieu de SN^*_ρ, SN^*_σ'.
In (46) the handwritten 'SN'_ρ, SN'_σ' corresponds to SN^*_ρ, SN^*_σ in the diagram; 'Cent_{𝔊^+}(ρ)', 'Cent_{𝔊^+}(σ)'.
Line 1: 'Les notations ε_γ, ε'_γ : Γ_{ρ,σ} → {±1} prêtent à confusion, la première signifiant l'action d'un γ sur L_σ (au lieu de L_ρ)'.
Diagram label on the dashed maps: δ_Z, δ_ρ, δ_σ; the character map is labelled (χ_γ, ε_{γ,ρ}, ε_{γ,σ}).
